summary: The candidate gives a broad, mostly faithful 40-entry extraction covering the main surgery, ribbon-category, modular-category, purification, RT, Jones, and root-of-unity narrative. However, it omits several verified supporting entries, merges distinct gold concepts, misclassifies multiple claims as definitions or calculations, lacks explicit per-entry attribution metadata, and includes a questionable Rohlin/surgery attribution.
strengths: Captures the principal results, including Lickorish–Wallace surgery, Kirby calculus, the Turaev ribbon-graph functor, Turaev purification, and the Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant.

Most mathematical statements and displayed formulas are faithful, including the ribbon Hopf convention, quantum trace, modular-category conditions, Kirby color, D/Delta normalization, and the RT surgery formula.
Page locators are present and generally align with the source, and the extraction also covers the later Jones-polynomial and root-of-unity discussion.
issues: Completeness gaps include the Kirby-reduction proposition, the Hopf-algebra definition, coproduct/antipode/R-matrix/universal-twist lemmas, separate finite-simple-system and Hopf-link-matrix entries, modular-data definition, purification-to-modular-category proposition, handle-slide and ±1 blowup lemmas, and presentation-independence proposition.
The negligible entry captures negligible modules but omits the gold definition of negligible morphisms; several other gold concepts are only partially represented through broad merged entries.

Classification is inconsistent with the gold: colored framed-link invariant is typed as a definition instead of a proposition, quantum trace as a definition instead of a lemma, and the D/Delta and normalization entries as calculations instead of the corresponding gold definitions.
Per-entry sourceReference, sourcePath/section anchors, and proof-status attribution are not preserved, making external results such as Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby, and Turaev less auditable.

The Rohlin entry folds the stronger surgery-by-2-handles conclusion into the cobordism theorem, which is a questionable attribution; the root-of-unity WRT entry also omits the requisite order and semisimplicity conditions.
The categorical-trace formula has ambiguous composition/tensor-product grouping because the tensor product of morphisms is not explicitly parenthesized.
